must_remember: EMF is not a force; it is the work done per unit charge in driving charge through the complete circuit, measured in volts.
The open-circuit terminal voltage of a cell equals its EMF because no internal voltage drop ($Ir$) occurs when current is zero.
During discharge, the terminal voltage is given by $V = E - Ir$, whereas during charging, it is $V = E + Ir$.
Maximum power is transferred to an external load when the load resistance equals the internal resistance ($R = r$), achieving an efficiency of $50\%$.
Internal resistance $r$ arises due to the resistivity of the internal electrolytic or structural components of the source.

glossary.meaning: The energy supplied by a source per unit charge, representing the potential difference across terminals on open circuit.
The opposition offered by the internal material and electrolyte of a source to the flow of electric current.
The actual potential difference across the external terminals of a source when current is flowing through the circuit.
The ratio of useful power delivered to the external load to the total power generated by the source, expressed as $\frac{R}{R+r}$.
